parts.what_went_wrong: Picked a direction from weight or drag alone instead of adding a small drag opposing motion to the large downward weight.
parts.fix: Draw both force arrows tip-to-tail; a small drag opposite to velocity only tilts the resultant slightly from vertical.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not use the rule that three non-parallel forces in equilibrium must meet at one point, nor that the cable joins at the centre of gravity.
parts.fix: For three-force equilibrium, extend lines of action to a common point; note where the weight acts on a uniform rod.

parts.what_went_wrong: Took only the braking triangle under the v-t graph, giving braking distance rather than stopping distance.
parts.fix: Stopping distance = thinking + braking: take the whole area under the v-t graph, rectangle plus triangle.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did long calculations with the time instead of noticing the question asked for rate of change of momentum, which is just the force.
parts.fix: Recognise rate of change of momentum equals resultant force, and kg m s^-2 is the newton, before calculating anything.

parts.what_went_wrong: Described light gates instead of the ruler and stopwatch given, and did not use v = 2s/t from rest.
parts.fix: Use only the apparatus named; from rest with uniform acceleration, final speed is twice the mean speed (s/t).

parts.what_went_wrong: Treated the oscilloscope x-axis as distance and talked about wavelength rather than reading the period.
parts.fix: Oscilloscope x-axis is time: period = divisions per cycle × time-base, then f = 1/T.

parts.what_went_wrong: Mentioned destructive interference but never used the resultant amplitude from (b)(i) or linked it to intensity.
parts.fix: Chain it: resultant amplitude (use previous part) → intensity ∝ amplitude² → state the intensity change.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave general interference talk without using the distances and wavelength; confused phase difference with path difference.
parts.fix: Calculate the path difference from the data, compare it to λ (here λ/2), then conclude destructive.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave the generic rectangular-block sin i/sin r practical, with the critical angle drawn in air or unclear.
parts.fix: For a semicircular block: aim ray at the centre, increase angle until refracted ray grazes the flat face; mark C inside glass to normal; n = 1/sin C.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used πr² or (4/3)πr³ instead of the sphere's surface area 4πr² when dividing power.
parts.fix: Intensity at a star's surface = power ÷ surface area of a sphere, 4πr².

parts.what_went_wrong: Found torque, or the work by one force only, instead of total work by the couple over one revolution.
parts.fix: Work by a couple = torque × angle turned in radians (2π per revolution); include both forces.

parts.what_went_wrong: Ignored constant volume, so only scaled length; missed that area falls by the same factor so R ∝ L².
parts.fix: When a wire is stretched at constant volume, A ∝ 1/L, so R scales with the square of the length factor.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not combine P = Fv with drag ∝ v² to obtain power ∝ v³.
parts.fix: Substitute one proportionality into another: P = Fv and F ∝ v² give P ∝ v³.

parts.what_went_wrong: Wrote momentum for moment, or said no forces act or constant speed.
parts.fix: Learn both equilibrium conditions exactly: zero resultant force and zero resultant moment about any point.

parts.what_went_wrong: Named the ball or table as feeling the partner of the ball's weight.
parts.fix: N3 pairs act on different bodies and are the same type: Earth pulls ball, ball pulls Earth.

parts.what_went_wrong: Treated weight and normal contact force on the ball as a Newton's third law pair.
parts.fix: Check N3 pairs: same type of force, acting on two different objects; W and N both act on the ball.

parts.what_went_wrong: Subtracted speeds on rebound instead of adding, used the wrong time or the ball's weight.
parts.fix: On rebound, take a positive direction: Δv = v - (-u), so speeds add; convert ms to s.

parts.what_went_wrong: Omitted normals, measured angles from the block surface, or switched to a critical-angle method.
parts.fix: Draw normals, measure i and r from the normal with a protractor, use n = sin i/sin r and plot sin i vs sin r.

parts.what_went_wrong: Claimed the factor of 2 came from sound travelling to the wall and back instead of λ = 2L.
parts.fix: Derive it: v = fλ with λ = 2L gives f = (v/2)(1/L); compare with y = mx explicitly.

parts.what_went_wrong: Suggested repeats and averaging, which does not reduce the uncertainty in a small measured length.
parts.fix: To cut % uncertainty in a small length, make it bigger: lower frequency or measure across several node spacings.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not recall the order of magnitude of ultraviolet wavelengths.
parts.fix: Memorise EM spectrum wavelength orders: UV about 10^-8 to 4×10^-7 m, visible 400–700 nm.

parts.what_went_wrong: Could not convert a 270° phase difference into a path difference of three-quarters of a wavelength.
parts.fix: Phase difference/360° = path difference/λ: 270° means 0.75λ = 3.0 cm here.

parts.what_went_wrong: Stopped at the useful output power instead of dividing by efficiency to get input power.
parts.fix: Underline which power is asked for; input = useful output ÷ efficiency.

parts.what_went_wrong: Just doubled the extension instead of scaling by L and 1/E together.
parts.fix: Write x = FL/(AE) and apply each factor: 1.5 × (1/3) = 0.5, so extension halves.

parts.what_went_wrong: Equated a weight to a moment instead of balancing two moments.
parts.fix: Balance moments: F × x = W × d, so with W, d fixed, x ∝ 1/F.

parts.what_went_wrong: Found only the horizontal tension component or only ma, without combining them to get the resistance.
parts.fix: Resolve, then write resultant force = component − resistance = ma, and solve for the unknown.

parts.what_went_wrong: Blamed losses to surroundings and missed that the clown also gains gravitational PE between A and B.
parts.fix: List every energy store that changes between the two points, including GPE if height changes.

parts.what_went_wrong: Recited 'action and reaction' without using the gradients of the momentum–time graphs.
parts.fix: Link gradient of p-t to force; state the gradients are equal in size and opposite in sign.

parts.what_went_wrong: Said the waves are not moving instead of naming fixed nodes and antinodes.
parts.fix: Identify a stationary wave by its features: nodes and antinodes at fixed positions.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave no actual way to measure frequency and no accuracy improvement.
parts.fix: Name a concrete method (signal generator tuned to resonance, or microphone + oscilloscope f = 1/T) plus one matching refinement.

parts.what_went_wrong: Combined uncertainties but ignored the instruction to give the answer to 2 s.f.
parts.fix: Double the % for a squared term, add %, convert to absolute, then obey the stated s.f.

parts.what_went_wrong: Drew a straight proportional line for a variable potential divider, or left it blank.
parts.fix: Reason about end values and how resistance ratio changes; non-linear dividers give curves, not straight lines.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not see that removing BC puts wire and resistor in series; mixed up p.d. across wire and resistor.
parts.fix: Redraw the circuit after the change, identify series/parallel, then apply the potential divider rule.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used a lamp's resistance for the wire, did not subtract lamp p.d.s, or left mm² unconverted.
parts.fix: Find the p.d. across the wire itself first; then R = V/I; convert mm² to m² (×10^-6) before ρ = RA/L.

parts.what_went_wrong: Forgot to convert the work function from eV to J before using λ = hc/φ.
parts.fix: Convert eV to J (×1.60×10^-19) before mixing with h and c; then convert m to nm.

parts.what_went_wrong: Took the photon energy as the electron's KE and skipped finding momentum before λ = h/p.
parts.fix: KEmax = hf − φ; then convert to J, find p = √(2mE), then λ = h/p.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used the textbook value of h instead of the measured gradient as instructed.
parts.fix: When told to use the gradient, use your measured value and find φ from the line's intercept.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not know that microwave wavelengths are on the scale of centimetres.
parts.fix: Memorise EM wavelength orders and convert to the units in the options (microwaves ~mm to cm).

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not calculate the critical angle (≈42°) and compare it with 45° to see total internal reflection.
parts.fix: Always compute sin C = 1/n and compare with the angle of incidence before choosing the ray path.

parts.what_went_wrong: Believed equilibrium means at rest, or that two balanced forces on one object form an N3 pair.
parts.fix: Equilibrium means zero resultant force (could be moving at constant velocity); N3 pairs act on different objects.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave only a qualitative comparison, or a raw difference, not compared with the % uncertainty.
parts.fix: Compute % difference from the accepted value and compare it with your % uncertainty; state consistent or not.

parts.what_went_wrong: Blamed frequency, phase or noise instead of unequal incident and reflected amplitudes.
parts.fix: Nodes are zero only if the two waves have equal amplitude; explain why amplitudes differ and how that varies with position.

parts.what_went_wrong: Said 'repeat' without saying average, or suggested non-specific changes.
parts.fix: Say 'repeat and calculate a mean', or better: measure across several node spacings to reduce % uncertainty.

parts.what_went_wrong: Said more intensity gives more electrons without linking photon rate, one-to-one interaction and current.
parts.fix: Build the chain: intensity ∝ photons per second → one photon frees one electron → current = charge per second.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used P = VI with the battery instead of photon energy × photons per second.
parts.fix: Power of a beam = energy per photon × photons per second; then intensity = power/area.

parts.what_went_wrong: Wrote vague 'human error' and 'more accurate' without using the 0.1 s intervals in the table.
parts.fix: Quote the data: compare the time intervals with reaction time (~0.2 s); mention replay frame by frame.

parts.what_went_wrong: Suggested repeat-and-average instead of a precaution such as avoiding parallax.
parts.fix: Give a specific precaution: camera level with and perpendicular to the scale to avoid parallax.

parts.what_went_wrong: Calculated distances or an overall average speed without showing the speed is constant.
parts.fix: To show terminal velocity, calculate speed for two later intervals and show they are equal.

parts.what_went_wrong: Forgot the square root, did not double radius to diameter, or mishandled mm↔m, so chose the wrong soil.
parts.fix: Rearrange carefully, check what quantity is asked (diameter vs radius), and convert units before classifying.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not know that the ampere is the only SI base unit among electrical units.
parts.fix: Learn the six SI base units: kg, m, s, A, K, mol; volt, ohm and coulomb are derived.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used the 9 mm span of six fringes as the fringe spacing instead of 1.5 mm.
parts.fix: Fringe width is between adjacent bright fringes: divide the total span by the number of spacings.

parts.what_went_wrong: Chose a definition of e.m.f. as energy per volt rather than energy per unit charge.
parts.fix: Learn e.m.f. exactly: energy transferred into electrical form per unit charge (per coulomb).

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not compute the critical angle to check whether total internal reflection happens at P.
parts.fix: Compute C from sin C = 1/n and compare with the angle of incidence at the boundary.

parts.what_went_wrong: Mixed energy and p.d. ideas or discussed current only, without linking wasted energy to less power in the bulb.
parts.fix: Follow one chain: larger r → more lost volts/I²r heating inside → less p.d./power delivered to the bulb.

parts.what_went_wrong: Vague talk of centre of mass and 'stress' instead of perpendicular distance, moment and force.
parts.fix: Use the chain: perpendicular distance reduced → moment smaller → force on spine smaller.

parts.what_went_wrong: Named light gates without a timer/logger or did not link the improvement to reaction time.
parts.fix: State the full set-up (trap door + electronic timer, or video) and say which error it removes.

parts.what_went_wrong: Drew straight lines or a rebound to full height, treating the bounce as elastic.
parts.fix: On s-t graphs, gradient is velocity: curves for acceleration; inelastic bounce means lower maximum height.

parts.what_went_wrong: Definition lacked precise terms such as maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons.
parts.fix: Learn symbol meanings word for word, including 'maximum', 'kinetic energy' and 'photoelectrons'.

parts.what_went_wrong: Only restated threshold frequency or that no electrons leave, without comparing photon energy with work function.
parts.fix: Explain: each photon's energy is less than the work function, so no electron gains enough energy to escape.

parts.what_went_wrong: Calculated measured/accepted × 100% instead of the difference divided by the accepted value.
parts.fix: % difference = |measured − accepted| ÷ accepted × 100%.

parts.what_went_wrong: Many thought g does not affect upthrust (item later withdrawn, so no marks counted).
parts.fix: Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced = ρVg, so it depends on g.

parts.what_went_wrong: Took only a triangle or multiplied peak values instead of estimating the full area under the F-t graph.
parts.fix: Impulse = whole area under force–time graph: count squares or split into shapes, and mind the ms scale.

parts.what_went_wrong: Vague reasons such as 'dirt' without saying a residue would change the refractive index.
parts.fix: Link each precaution to the measured quantity: leftover liquid film changes the observed refractive index.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave light intensity, which does not affect refractive index, instead of wavelength or temperature.
parts.fix: Pick control variables that actually affect the measured quantity: refractive index depends on wavelength and temperature.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not state that tension stays the same or refer to the perpendicular distance changing.
parts.fix: For moments questions, state what is constant, what distance changes, and the effect on the other force.

parts.what_went_wrong: Only said the pattern shifts, missing lower intensity because only a component of polarised waves is detected.
parts.fix: Apply polarisation: rotated transmitter means the receiver detects only a component, so same pattern but weaker.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not scale speed with the square root of the kinetic energy ratio (350/100).
parts.fix: KE ∝ v², so v scales by √(new KE/old KE); add energies in eV first.

parts.what_went_wrong: Assumed zero velocity means zero acceleration at the lowest point of the dive.
parts.fix: At rest the drag is zero but upthrust still exceeds weight, so there is an upward resultant force and acceleration.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave the amplitude ratio 2.4 instead of squaring it for intensity.
parts.fix: Intensity ∝ amplitude²: square the amplitude ratio.

parts.what_went_wrong: Divided power by the electron charge instead of the photon energy.
parts.fix: Photons per second = power ÷ energy of one photon (hc/λ or from the given value).

parts.what_went_wrong: Wrote F = ma or 'force equals change of momentum', missing 'rate of'.
parts.fix: Learn N2 precisely: resultant force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not use the area under the F-t graph as change of momentum, so could not find the rebound speed.
parts.fix: Area under F-t = Δp; then final momentum = Δp − initial with signs, divide by mass.

parts.what_went_wrong: Ignored that the cable is 17 strands in parallel and made power-of-ten errors in area.
parts.fix: Note structural details (17 wires in parallel → total A or R scaled); convert mm diameter to m before squaring.

parts.what_went_wrong: Thought the grille polarises microwaves and ignored the stated starting orientation.
parts.fix: State the source is already plane polarised; read the start position, then explain block (parallel) vs pass (perpendicular).

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not divide the wavelength in air by the refractive index.
parts.fix: In a medium, frequency is unchanged so λ_medium = λ_air / n.

parts.what_went_wrong: Thought intensity changes maximum electron speed, or answered vaguely.
parts.fix: Photon energy depends only on frequency; intensity changes photons per second, so KEmax is unchanged.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not start the rebound line at −4.2 m/s or keep it parallel to the falling line.
parts.fix: After a bounce the velocity sign flips but acceleration is still g, so the line stays parallel.

parts.what_went_wrong: Discussed terminal velocity instead of describing a curve with decreasing gradient and lower final speed.
parts.fix: Describe the graph: gradient decreases with time (curve), lower final velocity reached later.

parts.what_went_wrong: Tried the pressure equation instead of upthrust = ρVg.
parts.fix: Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced: rearrange ρ = U/(Vg).

parts.what_went_wrong: Could not turn a fraction of a wavelength read from the graph into a phase difference in radians.
parts.fix: Phase difference = (Δx/λ) × 2π radians; read Δx and λ from the same graph.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used amplitude ratio for intensity, forgetting intensity ∝ amplitude².
parts.fix: Square each amplitude before taking the intensity ratio.

parts.what_went_wrong: Power-of-ten errors, did not find drag force as instructed, wrong unit for viscosity.
parts.fix: Follow the stated route (drag = weight − upthrust), keep SI powers of ten, and derive units from the formula.

parts.what_went_wrong: Drew refraction at the first surface and missed total internal reflection at both 45° faces; rays unruled.
parts.fix: Check normal incidence passes straight through, then compare 45° with C; draw rays with a ruler.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used 45° or 41° instead of the glass-to-oil critical angle formula with 90°.
parts.fix: For a boundary between two media, sin C = n2/n1 (refraction angle 90°).

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not draw the ray leaving into the oil bending slightly away from the normal.
parts.fix: Use the critical angle you just found: 45° < C so the ray refracts out, bending away from normal into lower n.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not link the much smaller battery current to lower wire temperature and lower resistance.
parts.fix: Explain resistance changes via current → heating → temperature → resistance of metal.

parts.what_went_wrong: Vague 'more accurate' or 'digital meters' suggestions with no specific method.
parts.fix: Suggest concrete improvements: vary current with a variable resistor, plot V against I, use meters of higher resolution.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used only the vertical velocity component for kinetic energy, ignoring the horizontal one.
parts.fix: KE uses the full speed: combine components with Pythagoras, or use energy conservation with initial KE + GPE lost.

parts.what_went_wrong: Chose a ruler or micrometer instead of vernier callipers for ±0.1 mm over that length.
parts.fix: Match instrument to resolution and range: ruler 1 mm, callipers 0.1 mm (to ~15 cm), micrometer 0.01 mm (to ~25 mm).

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not know what the gradient represented, used the non-linear region or mixed N/mm with GPa.
parts.fix: Write the equation as y = mx to identify gradient (AE/L); use the linear part and convert to SI.

parts.what_went_wrong: Could not apply polarisation to water waves or justify it with oscillations in one plane.
parts.fix: Plane polarised means oscillations in one plane only; check the direction of oscillation in the new setting.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not realise the open-switch voltmeter reading equals the e.m.f.
parts.fix: With no current there are no lost volts: open-circuit p.d. = e.m.f.; then r = (E − V)/I.

parts.what_went_wrong: Left out the work function or KE term, or brought in de Broglie momentum.
parts.fix: Photon energy = φ + KEmax (φ = hf0); then λ = hc/E. De Broglie is for the electron, not the photon.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not round to 3 s.f. or made power-of-ten errors when scaling r³ ∝ T².
parts.fix: Use ratios: r2 = r1 × (T2/T1)^(2/3); keep units consistent and give the s.f. asked.

parts.what_went_wrong: Referred to mass or 'gravity' instead of the point where the weight appears to act.
parts.fix: Define centre of gravity precisely: the point where the entire weight of the object appears to act.

parts.what_went_wrong: Marked C without showing the median construction, or did not convert using the scale.
parts.fix: Show construction lines (two medians from midpoints to vertices), measure, then apply the scale factor.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave no detail on outlining the block, marking rays with crosses or joining points.
parts.fix: Describe ray tracing step by step: narrow beam, dim room, draw around block, mark rays with crosses, join, use protractor.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not see the path from Q is the mirror image of the incoming path.
parts.fix: Use symmetry: reflection at Q reverses the geometry; ray exiting into air bends away from the normal.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave 500 Hz or a lower frequency, not knowing closed tubes have only odd harmonics.
parts.fix: Closed (one end) tubes: only odd harmonics f0, 3f0, 5f0.

parts.what_went_wrong: Said 'switch open' rather than stating the current is zero so no p.d. across r.
parts.fix: Translate the circuit state into physics: switch open → current zero → no lost volts → reading = e.m.f.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not see that removing a parallel branch raises total resistance and lowers current.
parts.fix: Removing a parallel resistor increases total resistance, so the supply current decreases.

parts.what_went_wrong: Said voltmeter reading stays the same, ignoring internal resistance.
parts.fix: Lower current means fewer lost volts (Ir), so terminal p.d. rises.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not use half the range for absolute uncertainty, or did not triple the % for d³.
parts.fix: Absolute uncertainty = half the range; a cubed quantity triples its % uncertainty; add the % terms.

parts.what_went_wrong: No arrow or arrow the wrong way for conventional current from the carriers shown.
parts.fix: Conventional current is the direction positive charge flows: opposite to electron flow.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not realise the large fixed resistor takes nearly all the p.d., so the reading barely changes.
parts.fix: In potential dividers, compare resistances: if one dominates, the other's p.d. hardly varies; quantify the reading.

parts.what_went_wrong: Omitted the friction force, using only the force to raise the trolley.
parts.fix: List every force the pusher must overcome (component of weight + friction), sum them, then P = Fv.

parts.what_went_wrong: Gave 0.036 N s by subtracting magnitudes, ignoring that L rebounds.
parts.fix: Choose a positive direction; Δp = p_final − p_initial with signs, so a rebound adds magnitudes.

parts.what_went_wrong: Did not use impulse = change in momentum of R to find its velocity.
parts.fix: Impulse on R equals its change in momentum; from rest, v = impulse ÷ mass.

parts.what_went_wrong: Just rearranged the Young's equation instead of describing measuring across n fringes with callipers.
parts.fix: Answer 'how measured' with instrument + technique: callipers across many fringes, divide by number of spacings.

parts.what_went_wrong: Found the speed in glass but stopped there instead of the wavelength.
parts.fix: Check the final answer is the quantity asked; λ_glass = λ_air/n directly.

parts.what_went_wrong: Included the thinking time in the deceleration time instead of only the braking interval.
parts.fix: Read the graph section where braking happens; a = Δv/Δt over that interval only, then F = ma.

parts.what_went_wrong: Described effects qualitatively without quantifying thinking and braking times and distances.
parts.fix: Quantify: thinking distance ∝ v, braking time ∝ v, braking distance ∝ v²; give numbers.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used the wrong forces and distances in the moments about the edge X.
parts.fix: Take moments about the pivot edge with perpendicular distances: F × height = W × half-width.

parts.what_went_wrong: Used 150 W instead of 0.150 kW, or seconds instead of hours, for a kWh cost.
parts.fix: For kWh: power in kW × time in hours × price per kWh.

summary.pattern: Wrong core models recur: Newton's third law pairs (weight vs normal force, equilibrium = at rest), intensity changing photoelectron energy, photon energy taken as electron KE, and gaps in recall such as SI base units, EM wavelengths and closed-tube harmonics.
top_fixes: Test any N3 pair claim: same force type, two different bodies.
Photon energy depends only on f; intensity sets photons per second.
Keep a one-page recall list: SI base units, EM spectrum orders of magnitude, closed-pipe odd harmonics.
Equilibrium means zero resultant force and moment, not necessarily at rest.

summary.pattern: Physics broadly right but key terms missing or swapped: momentum for moment, 'switch open' for zero current, 'stress' for force, mass for weight, F = ma for rate of change of momentum, 'waves not moving' for nodes.
top_fixes: Learn definitions word for word (N2, e.m.f., centre of gravity, KEmax).
Replace everyday words with the technical quantity the mark scheme wants.
Translate circuit or situation states into physics quantities (current zero, perpendicular distance).

summary.pattern: Candidates skipped a decisive condition or data item: constant volume, 17 parallel strands, the named apparatus, 'use the gradient', 2 s.f., the start orientation, or answered a nearby question (useful vs input power).
top_fixes: Underline every given condition and the exact quantity asked before writing.
Use the data, graph or previous part the question points to.
Use only the apparatus named and the method instructed.
Re-read the question against your final answer and its s.f.

summary.pattern: Explanations stopped one link short: intensity → photons per second → current, larger r → lost volts → less bulb power, perpendicular distance → moment → force; or a constant quantity was left unstated.
top_fixes: Write explanations as an arrow chain, one marking point per link.
Count the marks and give at least that many distinct points.
State what stays constant as well as what changes.
Finish with an explicit conclusion tied to the question.

summary.pattern: Standard physics (TIR, potential dividers, polarisation, energy stores, moments about an edge) failed to transfer to new set-ups like oil-immersed prisms, clown launchers, seabirds and soil particles.
top_fixes: Strip the context: name the underlying topic before calculating.
Redraw the set-up as a standard diagram (circuit, force or ray diagram).
List every force or energy store present, not just the obvious one.

summary.pattern: Long chains broke: stopping at useful power, speed in glass, torque or one component; skipping a check of the critical angle; not finding momentum before de Broglie.
top_fixes: Plan the chain from the asked quantity backwards before starting.
After each step ask whether this is the final quantity.
For ray questions always compute the critical angle first.
Keep full-precision intermediates and label each.

summary.pattern: Methods were generic or unworkable: wrong block type, no normals, light gates with no timer, ruler where callipers were needed, 'repeat' without mean, vague 'more accurate' meters.
top_fixes: Name the instrument and its resolution, matched to the precision needed.
Describe how each reading is physically taken (what is marked, measured, timed).
Pair each improvement with the error it reduces.
To cut % uncertainty, make the measured quantity larger (several spacings, many oscillations).

summary.pattern: Graph technique was weak: partial areas under v-t and F-t graphs, oscilloscope x-axis read as distance, gradient meaning not identified, wrong interval read, sketches without curvature.
top_fixes: Identify what gradient and area represent before using a graph.
Use the whole relevant area and the correct interval.
Read axis units and time-base or scale factors.
Sketch curves where acceleration is present and keep parallel lines for equal acceleration.

summary.pattern: Plausible but wrong equations were chosen: πr² for sphere area, P = VI for photon power, dividing by e not photon energy, pressure equation for upthrust, braking vs stopping distance.
top_fixes: Before substituting, say what physical quantity the equation gives.
Check the situation matches the equation's conditions.
Know the key distinctions: braking vs stopping, change vs rate of change, photon vs electron.

summary.pattern: Linked scalings were missed: R ∝ L² at constant volume, I ∝ A², v ∝ √KE, P ∝ v³, combined L and E factors, braking distance ∝ v².
top_fixes: Write the governing equation and apply each factor separately.
Square amplitude ratios for intensity; root energy ratios for speed.
Check whether other variables change too (area when stretching).

summary.pattern: Prefix and unit slips: mm² to m², eV to J, ms to s, W to kW and s to h for kWh, mm and GPa in Young modulus work.
top_fixes: Convert everything to SI on the first line of working.
For cost use kW × hours.
Estimate the answer's size to catch power-of-ten errors.

summary.pattern: Direction was ignored: rebounds handled by subtracting speeds, rebound v-t lines starting at the wrong sign, KE from one velocity component, resultant of weight and drag guessed.
top_fixes: Choose and mark a positive direction on every momentum or v-t problem.
A rebound makes Δv the sum of speeds.
Combine perpendicular components with Pythagoras before using speed in KE.

summary.pattern: Uncertainty work was mechanical but incomplete: half-range not used, powers not multiplied, % difference divided by the wrong value, consistency judged qualitatively.
top_fixes: Absolute uncertainty = half range; multiply % by the power.
% difference uses the accepted value as denominator.
Judge consistency by comparing % difference with % uncertainty, with numbers.
